chapter: Stranded on the road and John Kirby
title: A first 'rehearsal' that was all whiskey
summary: At the hotel the band, including Wallace Bishop, Billy Kyle and Jerry Blake, drank rather than rehearsed, with the alto book torn and dirty.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: So anyway, it was just a different type of music, dance music. So anyway, I said, 'Well, yeah...' You know, he told to be at the hotel, a certain hotel at 4 o'clock in the afternoon for rehearsal. And we're going to stay in this hotel; it's not the hotel we're working at. So okay, 4 o'clock. He says, 'Do you need any money to get there?' I said, 'No, I've got transportation. I can make it.' See, I didn't know nothin' about Kirby. I didn't know him. I had never worked for him. 'I got the transportation. I'll be there at 4 o'clock.'
So at 4 o'clock I was in the hotel in Washington, and everybody was there. Everybody was in the room. We're sitting around. Everybody had a glass in their hand...
Now, who was everybody? Was there O'Neil Spencer now on drums?

No. I'll tell you who was on drums. What's his name, Wallace Bishop was on drums. There was Billy Kyle on piano. There was Jerry Blake on clarinet. There was Kirby on bass. And a fellow we used to call 'Minnow,' Clarence Brewington, on trumpet. A nice group.
You didn't double at this point.

No, no, just alto. So here I am. I've come in. Well, being the new man, I just know they're going to get the books open and show me this-that-and-the-other. So Kirby said, "The book's over there." So I went over and I picked up the alto book. And boy, the music was all torn and dirty, filthy, like somebody had been wiping their feet on it and turning the pages with the feet. And I see there wasn't nobody else getting any books. They all had glasses. So somebody asked me would I have a drink. And I said, "Oh sure," and I got me a little taste. After one bottle would get empty, another would appear.

So I'm still waiting for somebody to call a rehearsal there. So while I'm waiting, I have another drink. Well, after the second drink, boy... When they poured a drink they'd almost fill up a water glass. And after the second drink, I felt so happy, I said, "I don't care if they don't rehearse; it's all right with me."
So here we are. Kirby, he's rumblin' about this-that-and-the-other, "blah-blah-blah, and you shouldn't do this, and this," one-thing-and-another. Nobody's paying him any attention whatsoever.
So all right. The day goes, and it's getting close to time to eat.
